name: Searing Collar
summary: At Skull Rock in Durotar, Searing Collars burn the Burning Blade cultists who wear them. The heated torcs help attune them to demonic power.

sections.title: Instruments of Corruption
sections.body:
The Burning Blade gathers at Skull Rock, just east of Orgrimmar, for dark rites. Cultists, neophytes, and thugs wear Searing Collars around their necks. The metal brands and sears their skin as they endure its heat.

Margoz, a hermit, studies the cruel devices. He suspects their burning and enchantments attune the wearers to demonic energies. What part do the collars play in the corruption spreading through orc society under the Horde’s nose?

faq.answer: Burning Blade cultists wear Searing Collars around their necks in rituals. The heated metal burns their flesh and helps attune them to demonic power.
Members of the Burning Blade hiding inside Skull Rock wear the collars. They include cultists, fanatics, thugs, apprentices, and neophytes.

faq.q: Why do the cultists burn their own flesh?
faq.answer: The Burning Blade uses the searing metal in its rituals. By enduring the burns and demonic enchantment, cultists attune their bodies and spirits to demonic power.

faq.q: Who wants to inspect the Searing Collars?
faq.answer: Margoz, an investigator camping in Durotar, collects Searing Collars to study their enchantments and uncover the Burning Blade’s influence.

angles.text: As a warlock, you may know Searing Collars as crude conduits that channel fel corruption into mortal flesh.
As an orc, finding cultists using these collars on Durotar’s doorstep is a grim reminder that the shadow of demonic servitude still lingers.
